targets_metric: U (utility_accuracy); the census names nine checkpoints that are pure selection/label errors with zero A/F content: seven top-k truncations where the gold record ranked 12th+ under a total-overlap sort, one spurious answer_redacted from per-record (not marginal) answer-denial accounting, one spurious no_memory from structural-only tombstone overlap. Every change is to which records are ranked/handled and how the label is derived, not to what policy permits.
expected_tradeoff: A is held at or below 0.0588 because no grant is widened and every additional release still clears RBAC/scope/tombstone gates -- the marginal-content qad change and content-first ranking keep the raised agent top_k safe from the answer_redacted/refuse false-positive that sank the earlier 8->21 cap experiment. F stays ~0 because tombstone gate-1 responsiveness for real content words is unchanged and grows no leak surface; the only deletions that stop being related are those whose sole overlap was digits/contact, which cannot reconstruct them. Small, bounded F cost is possible for queries that would have been answered only by reconstructing a deletion through a contact/digit phrase alone, which the benchmark should not reward.
retrieval_loop: In MemoryStore.retrieve, PASS 0 is responsiveness: records are scored once with the structural/content digest split (_is_structural_term on digit-runs and the __contact__ tag). PASS 1 builds candidates as (total_overlap, structural, seq, row). Change the PASS-1 sort so real-content overlap dominates: candidates sorted by (total-structural, total, structural, seq) descending, so sparse logistics/date gold records out-rank chatty rows that accumulate digit-run/contact overlap but share little real content. Cap semantics are untouched; retrieve(top_k=8/1) tests keep passing. In PASS 2, gate order stays tombstone -> RBAC -> scope, each denial recorded in its own list. Change the gate-2/gate-3 query_answer_denials accumulator to marginal-content accounting: walk candidates in ranked order, and as records are appended to allowed, collect their real-content term hashes (digests matching the query's content_hashes, filtered by is_structural=0). A denied record withholds something answerable only if its matching content digests include one not already in the collected allowed union; only then increment qad. This prevents ten same-vocabulary denied records from flipping a complete answer to answer_redacted when the allowed union already covers the required content, and it keeps the wider agent top_k (11 -> 16) from re-introducing that flip on the extra evaluated-and-denied candidates.
forgetting_mechanism: Active forgetting keeps the tombstone never doing a hard DELETE; it (a) moves the record's term digests from record_terms into tombstone_terms preserving the new is_structural flag, (b) purges record_terms so the index does not outlive the body, (c) shreds the per-record crypto key (crypto_keys.key_material=NULL, ciphertext zeroed, shredded_at audit stamp) for confidential rows or overwrites plaintext body to '' for routine rows. Gate 1 of retrieve recognizes a deletion as related only when the tombstoned record shares a REAL content digest (is_structural=0) with the query; structural-only overlap (phone digit-runs, __contact__ tag) no longer forces no_memory. When preserved digests cannot scope (zero real-content rows captured) the conservative _DEFAULT_OVERLAP fallback remains, so a deleted record whose content is unknowable still reads as no_memory. F-probes query deleted facts by their own content words and therefore retain real-content overlap and still trigger no_memory.
